builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CSO: Refining Robotic Policies via Skill Distribution Alignment and Skill-Grained Optimization
summary: CSO replaces direct RL fine-tuning of VQ-VAE-discretized robot policies with a two-stage scheme: rejection-sampling supervised fine-tuning to align the observation-to-skill prior with successful trajectories, then skill-grained clipped policy optimization with the encoder frozen. It requires an online trajectory collection and rejection-sampling loop plus a pretrained QueST-style policy, adding pipeline complexity and dependence on successful rollout data rather than inference cost. It can fail when online collection yields few successful trajectories, when the frozen encoder is misaligned with deployment observations, or on tasks whose skill granularity mismatches the per-skill importance-ratio assumption.
rationale: This is a robot-manipulation policy refinement method requiring simulators, physical arms, and online trajectory collection, none of which applies to an LLM-focused production stack with a single GPU.
technique: Skill-aligned two-stage RL post-training for VQ robot policies

claims.statement: CSO replaces direct RL fine-tuning of VQ-VAE-discretized robot policies with a two-stage scheme: rejection-sampling supervised fine-tuning to align the observation-to-skill prior with successful trajectories, then skill-grained clipped policy optimization with the encoder frozen. It requires an online trajectory collection and rejection-sampling loop plus a pretrained QueST-style policy, adding pipeline complexity and dependence on successful rollout data rather than inference cost. It can fail when online collection yields few successful trajectories, when the frozen encoder is misaligned with deployment observations, or on tasks whose skill granularity mismatches the per-skill importance-ratio assumption.
Raises overall LIBERO success rate from 80.1% to 97.5% and achieves 61.0% success across five physical single-arm tasks; the claim is in percentage points, not a multiplicative factor.
